description: You are a P&C Actuarial Analyst at an insurance company completing the annual reserve review for the Workers Compensation line of business. The workbook 'workers_comp_triangle.xlsx' on your Desktop (ExcelTasks folder) contains three sheets. 'Triangle' shows cumulative paid loss data ($000s) for accident years 2019-2023 across five development periods (12, 24, 36, 48, 60 months) in NAIC Schedule P format. 'LDF_Development' has accident years pre-filled in rows 4-8, the tail factor (1.025) in cell B12, and a CDF-to-Ultimate breakdown table in rows 15-20; all LDF formula cells are blank. 'IBNR_Reserve' has current paid losses pre-filled in column B; all other columns are blank. Complete the following: (1) In 'LDF_Development', for each accident year and each adjacent development period pair where both values exist, calculate the age-to-age LDF (later period divided by earlier period) — this gives a table of individual LDFs in rows 4-8. (2) In row 10 ('Volume-Weighted Average LDF'), calculate the volume-weighted average for each period column using the formula: SUM of the later-period values across all eligible accident years divided by SUM of the corresponding earlier-period values (reference the Triangle sheet directly). (3) Complete the CDF-to-Ultimate table (rows 16-20): for each accident year, multiply the applicable remaining volume-weighted LDFs in sequence through to 60 months, then multiply by the tail factor in B12. For AY 2019 (at 60 months) the CDF = tail factor only. (4) In 'IBNR_Reserve', for each accident year: populate CDF-to-Ultimate from the LDF_Development sheet, calculate Projected Ultimate = Current Paid × CDF, calculate IBNR Reserve = Projected Ultimate - Current Paid, calculate IBNR % of Ultimate = IBNR / Projected Ultimate × 100, and set the Adequacy Flag to 'UNDER_RESERVED' if IBNR % exceeds 20%, otherwise leave blank. (5) In row 10 of 'IBNR_Reserve', sum the Current Paid, Projected Ultimate, and IBNR Reserve columns. Save the file using Ctrl+S.

metadata.occupation: P&C Insurance Actuaries / Loss Reserve Analysts
